_comment: Central calibration for the FAAB recommendation engine
(src/trade/faab_engine.py).  EVERY tunable lives here — the engine
contains no numeric literals that affect a recommendation.
Two quantities are computed and must never be conflated:
objectiveCeiling  what the player is worth, as a share of the
league's ORIGINAL full-season budget.  Depends
on the player and the league FORMAT only.  It
does not move when a manager spends.
recommendedBid    what THIS team should actually bid, given its
budget, roster, the drop side, the week, and
the expected competition.  Almost always well
below the ceiling.
See docs/faab-model.md for the derivation of every number below.
The value→FAAB curve is pinned between two league-format-derived
anchors, recomputed per league and per board refresh.  Neither is
a hard-coded value or player.
V_allin  — board value at rank (teamCount x startersPerTeam x
allinSlotMultiple): the size of the league-wide
STARTING pool.  A player at this line would start for
every team in the league, which is the scarcity level
at which committing the whole budget becomes rational.
Measured 2026-08-04: dynasty_main (12 teams x 20
starters = 240) -> 2341.  dynasty_new (10 x 10 = 100)
-> 3901, which is exactly Josh Jacobs, the value the
site owner independently named as an all-in player.
V_repl   — what you can add for free instead.  Format line at
replacementSlotMultiple x starter slots, blended with
the live pool's Nth-best unrostered player.  Measured
2026-08-04: format line (2.0x = rank 480) = 1383, live
12th-best free agent = 1668 — the two independent
estimates converge, which is why both are used.
s = (V - V_repl) / (V_allin - V_repl), clamped at 0.
displayed ceiling = smootherstep(min(1, s^toeExponent)).
smootherstep (6x^5 - 15x^4 + 10x^3) has ZERO slope at both ends,
so the curve cannot jump at either threshold — requirement 6/7
of the brief.  toeExponent > 1 lengthens the flat replacement-
level toe so ordinary wire players stay near zero; 2.2 was chosen
because it puts the real 2026-08-04 wire top (Marlin Klein,
1908) at a 5% ceiling against the LIVE blended anchors
(V_repl 1525.5, V_allin 2341) and ~12% against the format-only
anchors (V_repl 1383) the backtest uses, with the live
12th-best free agent at ~0% either way — while every
human-anchored all-in player still saturates at 100%.
Above V_allin the DISPLAYED ceiling stays capped at 100% of the
original budget, but an uncapped rawCeiling keeps growing
linearly (aboveAllinSlope per band-width).  The market layer
reads rawCeiling so it can still tell a 2400 player from a 9999
player; without it every saturated player would draw the same
recommended bid.  rawCeilingCap bounds it so the optimiser
cannot be driven to all-in by an unbounded number.
The cost of a drop is only the part of the dropped player that
is NOT re-acquirable from the wire: max(0, V_drop - V_repl).
Dropping a below-replacement player is free.  An open roster
spot means no drop at all.  Expressed as surplus so it subtracts
cleanly from the add's surplus with no double counting.
dropSurplusWeight ships at 1.0: the drop is charged its FULL
surplus over replacement.  A value below 1.0 would say the
dropped player retains some trade/stash worth you keep by not
making the claim, which is true but unmeasured here — and the
conservative direction is to charge the whole thing, since
under-charging a drop is what produces bids on swaps that do
not improve the roster.
FAAB has option value: a dollar kept can win a later claim.  The
ceiling is scaled by an option-value factor that RISES toward 1.0
as waiver periods run out, because unspent budget expires
worthless.  This deliberately does NOT make players more
expensive late — it only relaxes the ceiling.  The recommended
bid still comes from the market model, so it rises late only if
rivals actually bid more.
optionValueEarly is the share of the ceiling available in week 1
(the rest is reserved for future claims); it reaches 1.0 at the
last meaningful waiver period.  A team that is mathematically
eliminated, or past the final waiver period, has no future use
for FAAB, so its factor is forced to 1.0.
carryover: when a league carries FAAB into the offseason or the
next season, unspent budget is NOT worthless and the late-season
relaxation is damped by carryoverRetention.
Contender / rebuilder does NOT re-weight the player's dynasty
value — that is already the canonical 1-9999 number and
re-weighting it here would double-count age and outlook.  It
adjusts only the URGENCY of converting budget into roster now:
a contender values an immediate starter upgrade more than a
preserved budget, a rebuilder the reverse.  Applied to the
option-value factor, never to the player's value.
Roster need scales the TEAM ceiling only, never the objective
value.  Positional SCARCITY is already inside the canonical
value (and inside the league-adjusted overlay when that lens is
active), so this factor is deliberately about THIS roster's
shape — how many startable bodies it has at the position —
and not about the position's league-wide scarcity.
starterHole   the team cannot currently field a starter there
need          thin, an injury away from a hole
neutral       adequately covered
surplus       already deep; the add mostly duplicates a role
_spareComment: Need is classified by STARTABLE DEPTH: how many players at the
position grade above the free-agent replacement line, against
how many the lineup must start (direct slots plus a share of
every flex that accepts the position).  spare = startable -
required.  Below 0 is a hole; below needSpareThreshold is thin;
at or above surplusSpareThreshold is deep.

_comment: Rival bids are modelled as a zero-inflated lognormal.  Measured
against this league's real Sleeper history (695 completed
waiver/free-agent adds across 2024-2026): the median winning bid
is $0 in EVERY canonical-value band, 45-64% of adds cost nothing,
and the p90 rises with value (3% of budget below 1200, 12.5% at
2100-2600).  Most claims are uncontested, so the correct bid is
usually very small — while a genuinely contested claim has a long
right tail (observed max 52% of budget).
engagement  P(a given rival bids at all).  baseRate is the floor
for a replacement-level player; it climbs with the
player's surplus toward maxRate and is scaled by that
rival's positional need and remaining budget.
sigma       lognormal dispersion of a rival's bid given they bid.
Fitted from the spread of observed nonzero bids.
medianShare a rival's median bid as a share of their own ceiling
— managers bid well below their true max, which is
exactly the behaviour this engine reproduces.
_crowdComment: crowdBlendWeight: how far to move the modelled rival price
toward what comparable leagues ACTUALLY paid for this player
scripts/fetch_crowd_faab.py).  Observed beats modelled, so the
weight is above 0.5 — but not 1.0, because the crowd sample per
player is small (often 1-6 claims), MyFantasyLeague-only, and
an anonymous crowd rather than a panel of experts.
This moves the MARKET only.  The objective ceiling is computed
before any crowd data is read and bounds the bid regardless: a
hype cycle can tell us a claim will be expensive, never that
the player is worth more.  Measured 2026-08-04: the wider
market's superflex+TEP median is 0.30% of budget with a p90 of
8.5%, which brackets this league's own 0% / 6% — the two
markets agree, which is why the blend is safe.
_trendingComment: trendingEngagementLift / trendingSaturationCount: Sleeper
'trending adds' as evidence a claim will be CONTESTED — never as
evidence a player is WORTH more.  Added 2026-09-01 alongside the
engine-unification fix (docs/faab-live-opportunity-model.md):
before this, the raw add count was fetched and displayed as a
factor row but never actually reached Stage E, contradicting
both this file's own prior documentation and
faab_recommender.py's docstring, which already claimed it did.
trendingSaturationCount is category C (documented reasoning, not
yet an empirical fit — no outcome data ties a specific Sleeper
add count to a specific bid result).  count/trendingSaturationCount,
clamped to [0,1], is the 'share' blended into engagement exactly
like crowd_share.  trendingEngagementLift is deliberately SMALLER
than crowdEngagementLift (5.0): an add-count is weaker evidence
than a comparable league's actually PAID price, so a viral add
spike can raise expected competition but never dominate it the
way a real cross-league payment does.  Both constants are
flagged for recalibration once data/faab/shadow_comparisons_*
accumulates real cases (Phase 6 of the Live Waiver Opportunity
rollout).

_comment: The recommended bid maximises EXPECTED SURPLUS,
argmax_b  P(win | b) x (rawCeiling_team - b),
not win probability.  This is what produces 'worth $100, bid $36':
bidding the ceiling captures zero surplus by definition, so the
optimum is always strictly below it.
conservative / aggressive are the same curve read at different
win probabilities so all four numbers stay mutually consistent.
riskPosture shifts only the target on that curve — it can never
push a bid above the ceiling.
minEdge: when the optimiser is indifferent across a flat region
(the usual case for an uncontested wire player) prefer the
CHEAPEST bid within minEdge of the optimum, honouring 'the
lowest rational bid'.
Read from the live Sleeper league settings when available
(waiver_budget, waiver_type, waiver_clear_days); these are
fallbacks only.  waiverType 2 = FAAB.  zeroBidAllowed reflects
that Sleeper accepts $0 claims, which is how roughly half of
this league's adds are actually made.
Weighted share of realised (non-missing) inputs, matching the
existing compute_confidence buckets so the UI contract is
unchanged.
The LIVE WAIVER OPPORTUNITY layer (src/trade/faab_opportunity.py,
full record docs/faab-live-opportunity-model.md).  Shadow-gated
behind the 'waiver_live_opportunity' feature flag as of
2026-09-01 — none of these constants affect a LIVE recommendation
until that flag is promoted from shadow to live.
opportunity_value = dynasty_value + retention(dynasty_value) x
short_term_surplus
retentionFlat is category D (explicitly provisional): flat 1.0
until the shadow-comparison log gives outcome data to fit a real
retention curve.  Everything else here is category C (documented
reasoning, not yet an empirical fit) — plain, legible bounds
rather than tuned constants, because nothing here has been
validated against a realized outcome yet.
depthRankSaturation: rank 1 (the starter) scores +1.0; a slot
this many ranks deep scores -1.0, linear between.  3 is a plain
'within two backups of the starter' bound.
eventMuSaturation: the summed decayed mu_pct (BDVM's own
structured-event projection-delta channel) that saturates the
events axis at +/-1.0.  0.20 mirrors DEPTH_CHART_PROMOTION's own
ontology mu_pct (0.10) doubled, i.e. two independently-confirmed
promotions before the axis maxes out.
availabilityGamesDeltaFloor: decayed games_delta (from
INJURY/SURGERY/SUSPENSION/ACTIVATED_RETURN events) beyond this
many games zeroes the whole short-term surplus, not just the
events axis — an unavailable player has no immediate opportunity
regardless of how good his role looks on paper.
shortTermSurplusScale: board-value points at mean axis score
+/-1.0.  250 is a documented fraction (~1/3) of this league's
measured V_allin-minus-V_repl band width (~700-800 on the
2026-09-01 board) — enough to move an at-replacement player
meaningfully above the wire, not enough for role evidence alone
to manufacture an all-in-tier claim.
Which EXTERNAL leagues' waiver prices may inform this league's
expected clearing price, and how fresh that evidence has to be.
Owner spec: docs/FAAB_MARKET_SIGNAL_NORMALIZATION_2026-08-14.md
sections 3, 5 and 7.  Methodology and the measurements behind
these numbers: docs/faab-external-market-comparability.md.
These decide COMPARABILITY, never worth.  The objective FAAB
ceiling is computed before any external observation is read and
no key here can move it.
allowMultiCopyLeagues  MyFantasyLeague's rostersPerPlayer > 1
lets the same player sit on several rosters at once,
so there is no waiver scarcity and claims clear near
$0.  Measured on the live feed 2026-08-18: 39 of the
106 rows the old gate admitted came from such
leagues, at a median 0.20% of budget against 1.00%
for single-copy ones.  An unstated value is excluded
too: silence is not evidence of exclusivity.
minOriginalBudget  a league whose entire FAAB is a couple of
dollars cannot express a price, only claimed / did
not.  Measured: 7 rows at a $1 budget, every one
teamCountTolerance  +/- teams still counted comparable.  An exact
match ranks a tier higher rather than being required,
because exact-only discards most of an already small
feed.
tepSeverityGap  KTC publishes tep as 0/1/2/3 (Off / TE+ / TE++ /
TE+++).  A gap this wide demotes a tier.
maxFileAgeDays  the accumulated ledger proves when it was
written, not that it is still current.  Past this the
market is reported STALE and refused rather than
served as today's price.  The feed itself is a ~5-day
rolling window and the fetch runs on the scrape
cadence, so a week of silence is a dead timer.
minClaimsForTier  below this a tier's sample is reported but not
treated as a standalone read.
TIERS ARE REPORTED, NOT WEIGHTED.  The owner spec is explicit
that tier weights are evidence-gated ("Do not invent final
numeric weights merely from these labels"), and no outcome data
exists to fit them yet, so a tier changes no number today.
